If we use the seed value template of '018e5000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001' as suggested, should we just create a Python script to replace the `uuid-gen` values with the seed values right before we create the DB schema?

design_decisions.decision: Use TEXT + CHECK constraints instead of PostgreSQL ENUMs

design_decisions.decision: Accept ORM-generated naming patterns as standard
design_decisions.rationale: Alembic/SQLAlchemy generates constraint names automatically. Renaming 100+ constraints to match idealized conventions provides no functional benefit and introduces migration risk. Production database uses ORM patterns: foreign keys as '<table>_<column>_fkey', indexes as 'ix_<table>_<column>', unique constraints as '<table>_<column>_key'. These patterns are consistent, discoverable, and align with SQLAlchemy/Alembic defaults.

functions.definition:
CREATE FUNCTION audit.log_changes_code_pk() RETURNS trigger
    LANGUAGE plpgsql
    AS $$
        DECLARE
            v_user_id uuid;
            v_actor_type text;
            v_tenant_id uuid;
        BEGIN
            -- Read user_id from session variable (set by application)
            -- Falls back to system UUID if not set (background jobs, migrations)
            v_user_id := COALESCE(
                NULLIF(current_setting('app.user_id', true), '')::uuid,
                '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid
            );
            
            -- Determine actor_type based on user_id
            IF v_user_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid THEN
                v_actor_type := 'system';
            ELSE
                v_actor_type := 'user';
            END IF;
            
            -- Safely extract tenant_id (handles tables without tenant_id column)
            BEGIN
                v_tenant_id := COALESCE(NEW.tenant_id, OLD.tenant_id);
            EXCEPTION
                WHEN undefined_column THEN
                    v_tenant_id := NULL;
            END;
            
            -- Insert audit event record capturing the change
            INSERT INTO audit.event (
                tenant_id,
                user_id,
                actor_type,
                entity_name,
                entity_id,
                action,
                old_values,
                new_values,
                occurred_at
            ) VALUES (
                -- Tenant ID (NULL for platform-level tables)
                v_tenant_id,
                
                -- User ID from session variable or system UUID
                v_user_id,
                
                -- Actor type: 'user' or 'system'
                v_actor_type,
                
                -- Use table name as entity type
                TG_TABLE_NAME::text,
                
                -- Extract entity ID from 'code' column (primary key for these tables)
                COALESCE(NEW.code, OLD.code)::text,
                
                -- Operation type: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
                TG_OP,
                
                -- Old values (for UPDATE and DELETE operations)
                CASE
                    WHEN TG_OP IN ('DELETE', 'UPDATE') THEN row_to_json(OLD)::jsonb
                    ELSE NULL
                END,
                
                -- New values (for INSERT and UPDATE operations)
                CASE
                    WHEN TG_OP IN ('INSERT', 'UPDATE') THEN row_to_json(NEW)::jsonb
                    ELSE NULL
                END,
                
                -- Timestamp of the change
                NOW()
            );
            
            -- Return the appropriate record to allow the operation to complete
            RETURN COALESCE(NEW, OLD);
        END;
        $$;

CREATE FUNCTION public.recalc_invoice_totals_fn() RETURNS trigger
    LANGUAGE plpgsql
    AS $$
        DECLARE
          _iid uuid;
        BEGIN
          -- Determine parent invoice id from NEW/OLD
          IF TG_OP IN ('INSERT','UPDATE') THEN
            IF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'invoice_line' THEN
              _iid := NEW.invoice_id;
            ELSIF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'invoice_line_tax_component' THEN
              SELECT il.invoice_id INTO _iid FROM invoice_line il WHERE il.id = NEW.invoice_line_id;
            END IF;
          ELSE
            -- DELETE
            IF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'invoice_line' THEN
              _iid := OLD.invoice_id;
            ELSIF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'invoice_line_tax_component' THEN
              SELECT il.invoice_id INTO _iid FROM invoice_line il WHERE il.id = OLD.invoice_line_id;
            END IF;
          END IF;

          IF _iid IS NOT NULL THEN
            UPDATE invoice i SET
              subtotal_cents = COALESCE((SELECT SUM(subtotal_cents) FROM invoice_line WHERE invoice_id = _iid AND is_active = true), 0),
              tax_cents      = COALESCE((
                                  SELECT SUM(t.amount_cents)
                                    FROM invoice_line_tax_component t
                                    JOIN invoice_line l ON l.id = t.invoice_line_id
                                   WHERE l.invoice_id = _iid AND l.is_active = true
                                ), 0),
              total_cents    = COALESCE((SELECT SUM(subtotal_cents) FROM invoice_line WHERE invoice_id = _iid AND is_active = true), 0)
                                + COALESCE((
                                    SELECT SUM(t.amount_cents)
                                      FROM invoice_line_tax_component t
                                      JOIN invoice_line l ON l.id = t.invoice_line_id
                                     WHERE l.invoice_id = _iid AND l.is_active = true
                                  ), 0),
              balance_due_cents = (
                                    COALESCE((SELECT SUM(subtotal_cents) FROM invoice_line WHERE invoice_id = _iid AND is_active = true), 0)
                                    + COALESCE((
                                        SELECT SUM(t.amount_cents)
                                          FROM invoice_line_tax_component t
                                          JOIN invoice_line l ON l.id = t.invoice_line_id
                                         WHERE l.invoice_id = _iid AND l.is_active = true
                                      ), 0)
                                  )
                                  - COALESCE((
                                      SELECT SUM(p.amount_cents)
                                        FROM payment p
                                        JOIN payment_status ps ON ps.id = p.status_id
                                       WHERE p.invoice_id = _iid
                                         AND ps.code = 'completed'
                                    ), 0),
              updated_at     = now()
            WHERE i.id = _iid;
          END IF;

          RETURN COALESCE(NEW, OLD);
        END;$$;

user.comment: Centralized authenticated identity. Represents a unique human being who can log in. This same table supports Pilot platform staff, tenant employees, and tenant customers (via the portal). Access rights are determined by relationship tables (tenant_user, contact), not just this record.

id.description: Primary key. Global unique identifier for the user's identity.

email.description: The user's primary email address, used as their login username and for SSO matching. Stored as citext to ensure case-insensitive uniqueness (e.g., 'Bob@example.com' and 'bob@example.com' are treated as the same account).

first_name.description: The user's given name, used for UI personalization and email greetings. Example: 'Bob'.

is_platform_user.description: If true, this user is an internal Pilot employee with access to global super-admin tooling across all tenants.

platform_role_code.description: FK to platform_role.code. Specifies the exact internal Pilot role (e.g., 'support', 'owner'). By constraint, this MUST be populated if is_platform_user is true, and MUST be NULL otherwise to prevent accidental privilege escalation.

password_hash.description: Cryptographic hash (Argon2id PHC format) of the user's password. It is nullable to cleanly support users who authenticate exclusively via Single Sign-On (SSO) providers like Google or Microsoft.

email_verified_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the user clicked a secure verification link sent to their email. If NULL, the email is considered unverified and certain actions may be restricted.

failed_login_count.description: Security counter for consecutive incorrect password attempts. Used to trigger brute-force protection (account lockouts). Resets to 0 upon a successful login.

locked_until.description: If failed_login_count exceeds the tenant's password policy threshold, this stores the timestamp until which all login attempts are automatically rejected.

password_updated_at.description: Tracks the last time the password was changed. Used by the backend to enforce password rotation policies (e.g., 'must change every 90 days').

require_password_reset.description: If true, the user is forced to change their password immediately upon their next successful login. Typically set by an admin or triggered by a suspected security breach.

mfa_enforced.description: If true, the user MUST complete a Multi-Factor Authentication challenge (e.g., entering a 6-digit OTP) after successfully entering their password. Can be mandated by tenant policy or enabled voluntarily by the user.

preferred_mfa_channel.description: Dictates where the system routes the MFA OTP code during login. Allowed values: 'email' or 'sms'.

totp_secret.description: Stores the encrypted seed/secret used for Time-Based One-Time Passwords (TOTP) via Authenticator apps (e.g., Google Authenticator, Authy). Nullable because it is only populated if the user actively configures an auth app. Must be encrypted at the application layer before saving.

is_active.description: Soft-delete toggle. If false, the account is disabled and login is completely blocked, but the record remains in the database to preserve audit history and foreign key integrity.

last_login_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful authentication. Useful for security auditing and identifying dormant accounts.

display_color.description: B3/A18: Hex color code for dispatch board avatar rendering, e.g. #3B43D6. NULL until auto-assigned via tech_color_service.

id.description: Primary key for the quote line.

quote_id.description: FK to the parent quote this line belongs to.

position.description: Used to maintain the visual sort/display order of lines as arranged by the user.

qco_line_type_id.description: FK to qco_line_type indicating if this is material, labor, discount, etc.

pricebook_item_id.description: Optional FK to the tenant's internal custom pricebook. Mutually exclusive with supplier_item_id.

description.description: Human-readable description of the item or service shown to the customer.

quantity.description: Amount being sold. Supports up to 3 decimal places for partial units (e.g., 1.5 hours).

unit.description: Unit of measure text (e.g., 'feet', 'hours', 'each') for display purposes.

unit_price_cents.description: Historical snapshot of the item's price at the exact moment the quote was generated.

unit_cost_cents.description: Task 1-C-2: Raw material or labor cost at the time the line was added. Enables pre-sale gross margin calculation: (unit_price_cents - unit_cost_cents). Nullable — not all line types require a cost basis (e.g., discount or note lines).

cost_source.description: Task 1-C-2: Origin of the cost value (e.g., 'supplier_catalog', 'labor_rate', 'manual'). Used for audit and traceability of the cost basis.

supplier_id.description: Optional FK to the supplier table if this line is tied to a specific vendor.

supplier_item_id.description: Optional FK to the exact supplier catalog item. Do NOT use this to fetch live prices for old quotes.

taxability_code.description: FK to taxability_code. Determines the tax rules applied to this line (e.g., 'TTPP' for taxable property).

tax_rate_pct.description: The aggregate tax rate applied to this line (e.g., 8.2500 for 8.25%).

tax_basis_cents.description: The amount of the subtotal that is actually subject to tax. (Sometimes partial amounts are non-taxable).

tax_amount_cents.description: The calculated tax amount for this specific line. (basis * rate).

tax_jurisdiction_code.description: The primary geographical code used to determine the tax rate (e.g., a state/county code or zip).

tax_as_of.description: Timestamp indicating exactly when the tax engine was called to calculate these values.

tax_source.description: Where the tax calculation came from (e.g., 'avalara', 'stripe_tax', 'manual', 'system_default').

total_cents.description: The grand total for this line (subtotal_cents + tax_amount_cents).

subtotal_cents.description: The base cost before taxes (quantity * unit_price_cents).

created_at.description: Immutable timestamp recording exactly when this audit row was created. From AppendOnlyMixin.

action.description: Consent lifecycle event. CHECK: attested | double_opt_in_sent | double_opt_in_confirmed | opted_out. Mirrors customer_sms_consent_audit vocabulary.

consent_text_hash.description: SHA-256 of the disclosure text shown to the owner at attestation.

ip_address.description: Request IP at attestation. Nullable because webhook-driven opt-out (STOP) has no request IP.

attested_at.description: Timestamp the consent event occurred (attestation, send, confirmation, or opt-out).

created_by.description: The user who triggered the audit row. From AppendOnlyMixin. FK → user(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT.

GiST exclusion constraint prevents overlapping effective periods for the same (fee_code, entity_type) pair.

id.description: PK.

fee_code.description: Fee code identifier (e.g. brand_registration, campaign_quarterly, surcharge_att).

entity_type.description: Entity type: 'standard' or 'sole_proprietor'. CHECK constraint enforced.

amount_millicents.description: C-B9: Fee amount in millicents (1 millicent = $0.00001). Replaces amount_cents.

effective_from.description: C-B9: Temporal validity start. Row is current when effective_to IS NULL.

effective_to.description: C-B9: Temporal validity end. NULL means the row is current.

created_at.description: Immutable timestamp recording when this record was created.

created_by.description: FK to user.id. Who created this record.

updated_at.description: Timestamp updated automatically via triggers.

updated_by.description: FK to user.id. Who most recently modified this record.

constraints.uq_carrier_fee_schedule_temporal: EXCLUDE USING gist (fee_code WITH =, entity_type WITH =, tstzrange(effective_from, effective_to) WITH &&)

One active row per invoice (partial unique index uq_invoice_signoff_one_active); re-capture supersedes the prior row. The signature PNG lives in S3 at signature_object_key; the row carries metadata only.

tenant_id.description: FK to tenant.id

signed_by_name.description: Name of the customer who signed.

signature_object_key.description: S3 object key for the signature PNG.

signed_at.description: When the customer signed (client-side capture time).

client_capture_at.description: Offline capture timestamp from the mobile client.

captured_by_user_id.description: FK to user.id — the tech who captured the signature.

superseded_at.description: Set when a newer signoff supersedes this row. NULL = active.

idempotency_key.description: Client-provided key for offline replay safety.

created_by.description: FK to user.id who created this record.

event.comment: Authoritative, unified audit trail for all data and security events. Append-only with an optional hash chain for SOC2/tamper-evident compliance.

id.description: Primary key. Uses bigserial for maximum write performance on high-throughput event streams.

occurred_at.description: Timestamp indicating exactly when the event happened.

tenant_id.description: FK to the tenant table. NULL indicates a global/platform-level event. UUID scopes the event to a specific tenant.

user_id.description: FK to the user who triggered the event. NULL if triggered purely by an automated system.

actor_type.description: Indicates the context of the user. Constrained to: 'system', 'user', 'platform', or 'external_webhook'.

user_role.description: The specific RBAC role the user was acting under at the time (e.g., 'admin', 'technician'). Crucial for historical context if roles change later.

ip.description: The IP address of the client making the request. Essential for security audits.

user_agent.description: The browser or client string making the request.

request_id.description: The HTTP request ID from your backend API framework. Used to trace multiple database events back to a single API call.

correlation_id.description: A broader tracing ID (like OpenTelemetry) that might span multiple microservices or background jobs.

idempotency_key.description: Prevents duplicate processing. If a webhook fires twice, the idempotency key ensures you don't process it twice.

entity_name.description: The table or domain entity being audited (e.g., 'quote', 'user', 'invoice').

entity_id.description: The PK of the entity being audited. Stored as text to cleanly support both UUIDs and serial IDs without strict FK constraints.

old_values.description: The state of the row BEFORE the change. Null for inserts.

new_values.description: The state of the row AFTER the change. Null for deletes.

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason for the change, often captured from a 'confirm action' modal in the UI.

contextdata.description: Flexible payload for unstructured event data that doesn't fit standard columns.

prev_hash.description: Cryptographic hash of the PREVIOUS row in this table. Used to create a tamper-evident blockchain-style ledger.

self_hash.description: Cryptographic hash of THIS row's data...

hashed_at.description: Timestamp recording when the background Celery worker successfully computed the prev_hash/self_hash chain for this event.
